key_insight: Four-tetrahedron macro-element condensation shrinks interior-point Newton systems for equilibrium-based plasticity, enabling faster and more memory-efficient 3D solves.
engineering_relevance: The approach makes larger elastoplasticity and limit-analysis simulations feasible while retaining statically admissible stress fields.
method: Eliminate stress directions and macro-internal traction-continuity multipliers to form reduced systems compatible with positive-definite factorization.
Establish global and macro-local nonsingularity conditions, using trace-bound augmentation for von Mises limit analysis.
Use CUDA Fortran batched routines and cuDSS, with a lower-memory preconditioned conjugate-gradient option for elastoplasticity.
evidence_signal: Reported tests show up to 2× CPU speedup and 66.5% lower peak linear-solver memory versus stress-only elimination; the GPU implementation reaches up to 13.5× speedup over its CPU counterpart and 87.5× over MOSEK.
watch_item: The lower-memory iterative GPU solver increases solution time, and von Mises limit analysis requires trace-bound augmentation to ensure local nonsingularity.
paper_title: A GPU Interior-Point Solver with Macro-Element Condensation for Equilibrium-Based Plasticity
